title: Identify equal and unequal parts
concept: Recognise whether a whole has been split into equal parts before naming a fraction.
remediationNotes: Use concrete or visual reasoning first, then connect to the symbolic method.
recheckTemplates: Show a new partitioned shape and ask whether it can represent a fraction.
parentTutorNotes: Check that the child understands equal parts before naming a fraction.

title: Identify shaded fraction from a shape
concept: Write the fraction represented by shaded parts of one whole.
remediationNotes: Ask the child to count shaded equal parts first, then total equal parts.
recheckTemplates: Show a new shaded model and ask for the shaded fraction.
parentTutorNotes: Check whether the child counts the selected parts and the whole correctly.

title: Identify unshaded fraction from a shape
concept: Write the fraction represented by unshaded parts of one whole.
remediationNotes: Use shaded and unshaded counting together so the child sees both as parts of the same whole.
recheckTemplates: Show a shape and ask for the unshaded fraction.
parentTutorNotes: Good for checking whether the child understands numerator can refer to any selected part, not only shaded parts.

title: Identify fraction from a set
concept: Write the fraction of selected items in a set.
remediationNotes: Ask: how many items are in the full set, and how many are selected?
recheckTemplates: Give a new set of objects and ask for one category as a fraction of the set.
parentTutorNotes: Watch for children using only one subgroup as the denominator instead of the whole set.

title: Identify the whole in a fraction model
concept: Decide what counts as the complete whole in a diagram or context.
remediationNotes: Ask the student to point to or label one complete whole before writing the fraction.
recheckTemplates: Show a model with more than one possible visual group and ask what the whole is.
parentTutorNotes: Many fraction errors start from choosing the wrong whole.

title: Match fraction notation to model
concept: Connect symbolic numerator/denominator notation to a visual fraction model.
remediationNotes: Read the notation aloud as selected parts out of total equal parts.
recheckTemplates: Match a new fraction to one of several models.
parentTutorNotes: Use this to check whether the child connects notation to meaning, not only memorised format.

title: Explain numerator as selected parts
concept: Interpret numerator as the number of selected equal parts.
remediationNotes: Point to the top number and link it to selected or counted parts.
recheckTemplates: Ask what the numerator tells us in a new fraction model.
parentTutorNotes: A child may say numerator/denominator correctly but still not understand their roles.

title: Explain denominator as equal parts in the whole
concept: Interpret denominator as the number of equal parts in one whole.
remediationNotes: Point to the bottom number and link it to the total equal parts in one whole.
recheckTemplates: Ask what the denominator tells us in a new fraction model.
parentTutorNotes: Make sure the child says equal parts, not just total parts.

title: Identify unit fractions in models
concept: Recognise one equal part out of a whole split into equal parts.
remediationNotes: Show that unit fractions always have numerator 1.
recheckTemplates: Select the unit fraction represented by a new diagram.
parentTutorNotes: Unit fractions are important for comparison and fraction-of-quantity reasoning later.

title: Read fractions on a 0-to-1 number line
concept: Read fraction marks between 0 and 1.
remediationNotes: Count intervals, not tick marks, when reading a number line.
recheckTemplates: Read a marked fraction on a number line split into equal intervals.
parentTutorNotes: This is a common hidden weakness before mixed numbers and improper fractions.

title: Locate a fraction on a number line
concept: Place a given fraction on a number line with correct partitions.
remediationNotes: Partition the number line into denominator-sized intervals before locating the numerator.
recheckTemplates: Place a new fraction on a 0-to-1 number line.
parentTutorNotes: Ask the child to explain how many equal jumps make one whole.

title: Interpret fractions beyond 1 on a number line
concept: Read and place fractional values greater than one whole.
remediationNotes: Mark each whole interval first, then count fractional intervals beyond one.
recheckTemplates: Place a fraction greater than 1 on a number line.
parentTutorNotes: This bridges number-line understanding with mixed and improper fractions.

title: Compare unit fractions using denominator size
concept: Compare unit fractions by reasoning that larger denominators create smaller equal parts.
remediationNotes: Use same-sized wholes and show that more cuts make smaller parts.
recheckTemplates: Compare two new unit fractions using denominator-size reasoning.
parentTutorNotes: This should be explained conceptually, not memorised as a rule only.

title: Compare same-denominator fractions
concept: Compare fractions with the same denominator using numerator size.
remediationNotes: Show that the part size is the same, so the larger numerator has more equal parts.
recheckTemplates: Compare two same-denominator fractions.
parentTutorNotes: If this is weak, do not move too quickly into unlike denominators.

title: Compare same-numerator fractions
concept: Compare fractions with the same numerator using denominator size.
remediationNotes: Use same numerator examples to show that equal number of larger parts gives a larger amount.
recheckTemplates: Compare two same-numerator fractions.
parentTutorNotes: This is a common confusion because the child may think larger denominator means larger fraction.

title: Compare using benchmark one-half
concept: Use one-half as a benchmark to compare fractions.
remediationNotes: Ask whether each fraction is less than, equal to, or greater than one-half before comparing them.
recheckTemplates: Compare two unlike fractions by relating each to one-half.
parentTutorNotes: Benchmark reasoning reduces blind common-denominator work.

title: Order same-denominator fractions
concept: Arrange same-denominator fractions by numerator.
remediationNotes: Keep the denominator fixed and order by number of equal parts selected.
recheckTemplates: Order three same-denominator fractions.
parentTutorNotes: Ask the child to say why the denominator stays unchanged.

title: Order same-numerator fractions
concept: Arrange same-numerator fractions by denominator size.
remediationNotes: Show same numerator with same-sized wholes so the child sees which part size is bigger.
recheckTemplates: Order three same-numerator fractions.
parentTutorNotes: Useful before mixed unlike-fraction ordering.

title: Order mixed fractions using benchmarks
concept: Order unlike fractions using benchmarks, equivalence, or common denominators.
remediationNotes: Encourage a strategy choice: benchmark, common denominator, or equivalent fractions.
recheckTemplates: Order three unlike fractions with at least one near one-half.
parentTutorNotes: This begins to separate flexible reasoning from mechanical denominator work.

title: Recognise equivalent fractions in models
concept: Recognise same-size fractions shown with different partitions.
remediationNotes: Overlay or align same-sized wholes to show equal shaded amounts.
recheckTemplates: Show two new models and ask whether they are equivalent.
parentTutorNotes: The child should understand same value, not same-looking pieces.

title: Recognise equivalent fractions symbolically
concept: Recognise equality after scaling numerator and denominator.
remediationNotes: Show that multiplying or dividing both parts by the same number preserves value.
recheckTemplates: Ask whether two symbolic fractions are equivalent and why.
parentTutorNotes: Useful bridge from models to procedures.

title: Generate equivalent fractions by multiplying
concept: Multiply numerator and denominator by the same number.
remediationNotes: Circle the scale factor and apply it to both numerator and denominator.
recheckTemplates: Generate two equivalent fractions from a given fraction by multiplying.
parentTutorNotes: Watch whether the child changes both numerator and denominator.

title: Generate equivalent fractions by dividing
concept: Divide numerator and denominator by the same number.
remediationNotes: Show that division is the reverse of generating larger equivalent fractions.
recheckTemplates: Find an equivalent fraction by dividing both parts by the same number.
parentTutorNotes: This prepares for simplifying fractions.

title: Find missing numerator or denominator in equivalent fractions
concept: Find an unknown value using the same scale factor.
remediationNotes: Find the known scale factor first, then apply it to the missing part.
recheckTemplates: Complete a new equivalent-fraction statement with one missing value.
parentTutorNotes: If the child guesses, ask them to write the scale factor above the arrow.

title: Simplify using a common factor
concept: Reduce a fraction by dividing by a common factor.
remediationNotes: List or identify a common factor and divide numerator and denominator by it.
recheckTemplates: Simplify a new fraction using a visible common factor.
parentTutorNotes: This can be developed gradually before requiring HCF every time.

title: Simplify to lowest terms using HCF
concept: Use the highest common factor to express a fraction in simplest form.
remediationNotes: Find the greatest number that divides both numerator and denominator.
recheckTemplates: Simplify a new fraction where the HCF is greater than 1.
parentTutorNotes: Also use this to check whether the child leaves answers like 3/6 instead of 1/2.

title: Check whether a fraction is in simplest form
concept: Decide whether numerator and denominator have no common factor besides 1.
remediationNotes: Ask the child to check common factors before submitting final answer.
recheckTemplates: Show a fraction and ask whether it is simplest; if not, simplify it.
parentTutorNotes: This is an important final-answer habit for exams.

title: Interpret improper fractions as more than one whole
stage: Fractions III: Mixed Numbers and Conversion
concept: Understand improper fractions as one or more wholes plus extra parts.
remediationNotes: Count each denominator-sized part across all wholes.
recheckTemplates: Show more-than-one-whole shaded models and ask for the improper fraction.
parentTutorNotes: This prepares children to move between diagrams, improper fractions, and mixed numbers.

title: Represent improper fractions with models
stage: Fractions III: Mixed Numbers and Conversion
concept: Count shaded equal parts across multiple wholes.
remediationNotes: Label each complete whole as denominator over denominator, then add the extra parts.
recheckTemplates: Choose the diagram that represents a given improper fraction.
parentTutorNotes: Students often count wholes only and miss the total number of equal parts.

title: Interpret mixed numbers as whole plus fraction
stage: Fractions III: Mixed Numbers and Conversion
concept: Understand a mixed number as a whole-number part plus a fractional part.
remediationNotes: Separate the whole-number part from the fractional part before calculating.
recheckTemplates: Ask how many unit fraction parts are in a new mixed number.
parentTutorNotes: Good for detecting whether the child understands the whole part or only sees the numerator/denominator.

title: Represent mixed numbers with models
stage: Fractions III: Mixed Numbers and Conversion
concept: Show whole units and a fractional part using diagrams.
remediationNotes: Draw complete wholes first, then the remaining fractional part.
recheckTemplates: Choose or draw a model for a mixed number.
parentTutorNotes: Students should be able to explain why the fraction part comes from the same-sized whole.

title: Convert improper fraction to mixed number using division
stage: Fractions III: Mixed Numbers and Conversion
concept: Divide numerator by denominator to get whole number and remainder.
remediationNotes: Use quotient as whole number, remainder as numerator, and keep the same denominator.
recheckTemplates: Convert a new improper fraction to mixed number.
parentTutorNotes: Check whether the child places the remainder correctly.

title: Convert mixed number to improper fraction
stage: Fractions III: Mixed Numbers and Conversion
concept: Convert wholes into denominator-sized parts and add the numerator.
remediationNotes: Use whole × denominator + numerator, over the same denominator, and connect it to a model.
recheckTemplates: Convert a new mixed number into an improper fraction.
parentTutorNotes: A common error is adding the whole number to numerator only.

title: Compare mixed numbers and improper fractions
stage: Fractions III: Mixed Numbers and Conversion
concept: Convert or model values to compare quantities greater than one.
remediationNotes: Convert both values to the same form or compare using same-sized visual wholes.
recheckTemplates: Compare a mixed number and an improper fraction with different denominators.
parentTutorNotes: This skill checks both conversion and size reasoning.

title: Place mixed numbers and improper fractions on a number line
stage: Fractions III: Mixed Numbers and Conversion
concept: Represent values greater than one on a number line.
remediationNotes: Mark whole numbers first, then partition each whole into equal denominator-sized intervals.
recheckTemplates: Place a new mixed number on a number line and write the equivalent improper fraction.
parentTutorNotes: Useful for visualising value instead of relying only on procedures.

title: Add same-denominator proper fractions
concept: Add numerators while keeping the same denominator.
remediationNotes: Explain that the denominator names the size of each part, so it stays the same.
recheckTemplates: Add two like fractions with a proper-fraction answer.
parentTutorNotes: Adding denominators is a major sign that denominator meaning is weak.

title: Add same-denominator fractions with improper result
concept: Add like fractions and convert an improper result to a mixed number when required.
remediationNotes: After adding, check whether the result is greater than one and whether the question asks for mixed number form.
recheckTemplates: Add two like fractions whose sum is greater than one and express as mixed number.
parentTutorNotes: This catches children who compute correctly but do not follow the requested answer form.

title: Subtract same-denominator proper fractions
concept: Subtract numerators while keeping the same denominator.
remediationNotes: Show that the part size is unchanged, so subtract only selected parts.
recheckTemplates: Subtract two same-denominator fractions.
parentTutorNotes: If the child subtracts denominators, revisit denominator meaning.

title: Subtract same-denominator fractions from one whole
concept: Rename one whole as denominator over denominator before subtracting.
remediationNotes: Rewrite one whole as all denominator-sized parts before subtracting.
recheckTemplates: Subtract a fraction from one whole or a whole number.
parentTutorNotes: This is a key prerequisite for subtracting mixed numbers with regrouping.

title: Find a common denominator for two fractions
concept: Find a shared denominator before adding or subtracting unlike fractions.
remediationNotes: Find a common multiple and convert both fractions before operating.
recheckTemplates: Convert two unlike fractions to equivalent fractions with a common denominator.
parentTutorNotes: This is the hidden step behind most unlike-denominator operation errors.

title: Add unlike proper fractions
concept: Convert unlike fractions to a common denominator before adding.
remediationNotes: Do not add until both fractions describe same-sized parts.
recheckTemplates: Add two unlike proper fractions with denominator not exceeding 12.
parentTutorNotes: Ask the child to show the equivalent-fraction step.

title: Add unlike fractions and simplify
concept: Add unlike fractions and reduce final answer if needed.
remediationNotes: After adding, check whether numerator and denominator share a common factor.
recheckTemplates: Add unlike fractions where the result can be simplified.
parentTutorNotes: This separates computation accuracy from final-answer quality.

title: Add mixed numbers
concept: Add whole parts and fractional parts, regrouping if needed.
remediationNotes: Add wholes and fractions separately, then regroup if the fraction sum is improper.
recheckTemplates: Add two mixed numbers with and without regrouping.
parentTutorNotes: Alternative method: convert to improper fractions first, then add.

title: Subtract unlike proper fractions
concept: Convert unlike fractions to a common denominator before subtracting.
remediationNotes: Change to same-sized parts before subtracting numerator quantities.
recheckTemplates: Subtract two unlike proper fractions and simplify.
parentTutorNotes: Watch for students who subtract straight across numerator and denominator.

title: Subtract unlike fractions requiring regrouping
concept: Rename wholes or mixed numbers when the fractional part is insufficient.
remediationNotes: Borrow one whole and rename it as denominator-sized fractional parts.
recheckTemplates: Subtract a mixed number from a mixed number requiring regrouping.
parentTutorNotes: This often needs visual support before symbolic fluency.

title: Subtract mixed numbers
concept: Subtract mixed numbers with common denominator and regrouping strategies.
remediationNotes: Either subtract whole and fractional parts after common denominator, or convert both to improper fractions first.
recheckTemplates: Subtract two mixed numbers and explain the method used.
parentTutorNotes: This is a high-value skill for P5/P6 operations readiness.

title: Multiply a fraction by a whole number
concept: Find repeated groups of a fractional amount.
remediationNotes: Show multiplication as repeated addition of equal fractional groups.
recheckTemplates: Find a whole-number multiple of a proper fraction.
parentTutorNotes: This links fluency to fraction-of-quantity reasoning.

title: Multiply a whole number by a fraction
concept: Find a fractional part of a whole-number quantity.
remediationNotes: Find one unit fraction of the quantity first, then multiply by the numerator.
recheckTemplates: Find a non-unit fraction of a whole-number quantity.
parentTutorNotes: This is both an operation skill and an application skill.

title: Multiply a fraction by a fraction
concept: Find a fraction of a fraction and simplify the product.
remediationNotes: Use a visual area/strip model, then multiply numerators and denominators.
recheckTemplates: Multiply two proper fractions and simplify.
parentTutorNotes: If the child can calculate but not explain, use a visual model first.

title: Simplify before or after multiplication
concept: Use cancellation or simplify the final product.
remediationNotes: Show that simplification can happen before multiplying or after finding the product.
recheckTemplates: Multiply two fractions where simplification is possible before multiplying.
parentTutorNotes: This improves accuracy and reduces large-number errors.

title: Divide a whole number by a unit fraction
concept: Find how many unit-fraction groups fit into a whole number.
remediationNotes: Ask how many fractional groups fit into the total; connect to multiply by reciprocal after meaning is clear.
recheckTemplates: Divide a whole number by a unit fraction in a countable context.
parentTutorNotes: This is where children often memorise reciprocal without understanding context.

title: Divide a fraction by a whole number
concept: Share a fractional amount equally into whole-number groups.
remediationNotes: Show that dividing by a whole number means taking that fraction of the amount.
recheckTemplates: Divide a proper fraction by a whole number in a sharing context.
parentTutorNotes: This should feel like sharing, not only a reciprocal rule.

title: Divide by a fraction using reciprocal
concept: Multiply by the reciprocal to divide by a fraction.
remediationNotes: Connect reciprocal procedure to the question: how many fractional groups fit into the amount?
recheckTemplates: Divide a proper fraction by a proper fraction and interpret the result.
parentTutorNotes: Context decides whether a fractional quotient should be rounded up/down or kept as a fraction.

title: Find unit fraction of a countable quantity
stage: Fractions V: Fraction of Quantity and Model Drawing
concept: Divide a countable total into equal parts and find one part.
remediationNotes: Divide by the denominator to find one unit fraction of the quantity.
recheckTemplates: Find one unit fraction of a new countable total.
parentTutorNotes: Check divisibility and whether the answer should be a whole number.

title: Find non-unit fraction of a countable quantity
stage: Fractions V: Fraction of Quantity and Model Drawing
concept: Find one unit first, then multiply by the numerator.
remediationNotes: Use denominator to find one part, then numerator to find the selected parts.
recheckTemplates: Find a non-unit fraction of a new countable total.
parentTutorNotes: The child should not multiply by numerator before finding unit size unless using an equivalent efficient method.

title: Find fraction of a continuous quantity
stage: Fractions V: Fraction of Quantity and Model Drawing
concept: Apply fraction-of-quantity reasoning to mass, length, volume, or money.
remediationNotes: Keep units visible and convert units only when the question requires it.
recheckTemplates: Find a fraction of a length, mass, or volume with correct units.
parentTutorNotes: Good for detecting unit and answer-form mistakes.

title: Check countability constraints in word problems
stage: Fractions V: Fraction of Quantity and Model Drawing
concept: Check whether fractional answers make sense for countable items.
remediationNotes: Ask whether the answer counts people/items/containers, or measures a continuous quantity.
recheckTemplates: Give a countable-object problem and ask whether to round, keep fraction, or give whole number.
parentTutorNotes: This is important for P6 division word problems with containers, cups, and pieces.

title: Draw a part-whole bar model
stage: Fractions V: Fraction of Quantity and Model Drawing
concept: Represent a total split into parts using a bar model.
remediationNotes: Label the whole bar, known parts, unknown part, and unit value.
recheckTemplates: Draw a part-whole bar model for a new word problem.
parentTutorNotes: This should be practised as a separate skill, not only inside difficult problems.

title: Draw a remainder bar model
stage: Fractions V: Fraction of Quantity and Model Drawing
concept: Represent what remains after a fractional part is removed.
remediationNotes: Draw the original whole first, then label used/removed and remaining parts separately.
recheckTemplates: Draw a remainder model for a new fraction-used/fraction-left problem.
parentTutorNotes: A missing remainder model often causes students to apply the next fraction to the wrong whole.

title: Subdivide a remainder in a bar model
stage: Fractions V: Fraction of Quantity and Model Drawing
concept: Apply a fraction to a remainder rather than the original whole.
remediationNotes: After the first event, redraw or relabel the remainder as the new whole for the next fraction.
recheckTemplates: Solve a new fraction-of-remainder problem and label the new whole.
parentTutorNotes: This is one of the biggest jump points from P4 to upper-primary word problems.

title: Use branching/tree method for fraction-of-remainder problems
stage: Fractions V: Fraction of Quantity and Model Drawing
concept: Track sequential fraction-of-remainder relationships.
remediationNotes: Use a branch/tree to show each event and its remaining branch before calculating.
recheckTemplates: Solve a new sequential fraction-of-remainder problem using a branch diagram.
parentTutorNotes: This supports advanced P5/P6 work-backwards problems.

title: Identify what the question asks for
stage: Fractions VI: Word Problems and Heuristics
concept: Locate the target quantity and answer form before calculating.
remediationNotes: Ask the student to underline the final question and state what the answer should represent.
recheckTemplates: Give a word problem and ask only what needs to be found before solving.
parentTutorNotes: Many children calculate correctly but answer the wrong thing.

title: Identify the whole, part, and remainder
stage: Fractions VI: Word Problems and Heuristics
concept: Separate original whole, used part, leftover part, and comparison amount.
remediationNotes: Label the whole, known parts, unknown part, and remainder before choosing an operation.
recheckTemplates: Label whole, part, and remainder in a new word problem.
parentTutorNotes: This is the first adult review point for weak word-problem solvers.

title: Solve one-step part-whole fraction word problems
stage: Fractions VI: Word Problems and Heuristics
concept: Use addition or subtraction of fractional parts in a simple context.
remediationNotes: Decide whether parts are being combined or removed from the whole.
recheckTemplates: Solve a new one-step part-whole fraction word problem.
parentTutorNotes: Ask the child to say why the operation is addition or subtraction.

title: Solve one-step fraction-of-quantity word problems
stage: Fractions VI: Word Problems and Heuristics
concept: Find a quantity from a given fraction of a total.
remediationNotes: Find one unit fraction first, then scale to the requested numerator.
recheckTemplates: Solve a new fraction-of-quantity word problem.
parentTutorNotes: Check for denominator-first reasoning.

title: Solve remainder-after-giving-away problems
stage: Fractions VI: Word Problems and Heuristics
concept: Find what remains after one or more transfers.
remediationNotes: Track removed parts and remaining parts separately on a bar.
recheckTemplates: Solve a new give-away/leftover fraction problem.
parentTutorNotes: A child may report the amount used instead of the amount left.

title: Solve comparison fraction word problems
stage: Fractions VI: Word Problems and Heuristics
concept: Find how much more/less or compare fractions in context.
remediationNotes: Draw aligned bars and label the difference or comparison unit.
recheckTemplates: Solve a new more-than/less-than fraction comparison problem.
parentTutorNotes: Comparison model errors often look like arithmetic errors but are comprehension/model errors.

title: Choose the correct operation in a word problem
stage: Fractions VI: Word Problems and Heuristics
concept: Choose add, subtract, multiply, or divide based on the story structure.
remediationNotes: Identify whether the story combines, removes, compares, shares, or groups quantities.
recheckTemplates: Give a new word problem and ask which operation is needed before solving.
parentTutorNotes: This should be tracked separately from arithmetic accuracy.

title: Solve two-step fraction sequence problems
stage: Fractions VI: Word Problems and Heuristics
concept: Carry out two or more operations in sequence.
remediationNotes: Write step 1 and step 2 explicitly and check whether the final question has been answered.
recheckTemplates: Solve a new two-step fraction word problem with two answer parts.
parentTutorNotes: Students may stop after the first part, especially in multi-part contexts.

title: Solve fraction-of-remainder problems
stage: Fractions VI: Word Problems and Heuristics
concept: Apply a fraction to the remaining amount after an earlier action.
remediationNotes: After each action, define the new whole before applying the next fraction.
recheckTemplates: Solve a new problem where a fraction is taken from the remainder.
parentTutorNotes: This is a priority remediation target for upper-primary fractions.

title: Solve work-backwards fraction problems
stage: Fractions VI: Word Problems and Heuristics
concept: Use a final amount to reconstruct the original total.
remediationNotes: Start from the known final amount and rebuild unit values backwards.
recheckTemplates: Solve a new problem where the amount left is known and the original amount is required.
parentTutorNotes: Ask the student to label which quantity is known at the end and which is required at first.

title: Solve before-after fraction problems
stage: Fractions VI: Word Problems and Heuristics
concept: Track changes in a quantity before and after transfers or spending.
remediationNotes: Draw before and after bars and connect the known changed amount to units.
recheckTemplates: Solve a new before-after fraction problem with a known final amount.
parentTutorNotes: This should connect to model drawing and working evidence, not just final answer checking.

title: Check whether final answer matches the question
stage: Fractions VI: Word Problems and Heuristics
concept: Verify units, answer form, and whether all parts of the question were answered.
remediationNotes: Ask: Does my answer have the correct unit? Is it a count or a measure? Did I answer all parts?
recheckTemplates: Review a worked answer and decide whether it answers the question.
parentTutorNotes: This is especially important for P6 division contexts where rounding direction matters.

title: Mixed-format fraction skill check
stage: Fractions VII: Exam Applications and Mastery
concept: Check several fraction subskills in one short set.
remediationNotes: Route each error back to the weakest underlying micro-skill.
recheckTemplates: Give a short mixed-format set targeted to previously weak skills.
parentTutorNotes: Use this as a dashboard checkpoint, not as a teachable skill by itself.

title: Exam-style one-mark fraction items
stage: Fractions VII: Exam Applications and Mastery
concept: Answer direct exam-style fraction items accurately.
remediationNotes: Use these to identify careless answer-form and simplification errors.
recheckTemplates: Give a new one-mark direct fraction item.
parentTutorNotes: Good for fluency and accuracy, but not enough for model-drawing mastery.

title: Exam-style two-mark fraction items
stage: Fractions VII: Exam Applications and Mastery
concept: Show method for multi-step fraction questions.
remediationNotes: Require working evidence and route weak steps back to model type or operation skill.
recheckTemplates: Give a two-step problem with the same schema but new values.
parentTutorNotes: Use working evidence to decide whether the child guessed or had a valid method.

title: Method-mark fraction working
stage: Fractions VII: Exam Applications and Mastery
concept: Record clear working that shows the model or operation chain.
remediationNotes: Prompt the child to show the model, unit values, operation chain, and final answer check.
recheckTemplates: Ask the child to solve and upload/draw working for a similar model-based item.
parentTutorNotes: Do not treat answer-only success as full mastery for method-mark problems.

title: Multi-topic fraction problem solving
stage: Fractions VII: Exam Applications and Mastery
concept: Combine fraction operations with ratio, percentage, area, or word-problem schemas.
remediationNotes: Break the problem into known relationships, model type, and target answer before calculating.
recheckTemplates: Give a new multi-topic fraction application with a known model type.
parentTutorNotes: This should remain an assessment/application node, not a single teachable concept.

title: Fractions mastery checkpoint
stage: Fractions VII: Exam Applications and Mastery
concept: Demonstrate stable mastery across mixed fraction topics.
remediationNotes: Analyse error pattern across micro-skills rather than treating mastery as one topic.
recheckTemplates: Give a mastery set weighted toward previously weak micro-skills.
parentTutorNotes: This should summarise readiness, not replace targeted remediation.

title: Fractions remediation retest
stage: Fractions VII: Exam Applications and Mastery
concept: Retest weak micro-skills after targeted remediation.
remediationNotes: Select recheck questions based on the misconception tags from the previous attempt.
recheckTemplates: Generate a short recheck set from the same micro-skill but different surface context.
parentTutorNotes: Useful for proving whether remediation actually worked.
